body.text: Staying in isn't a failure to make plans. It can be the plan, provided you actually make it.

The difference is three small decisions: a start time, a little setup and a rule about your phone. Do those and the sofa becomes a venue. Here's how to set the scene, with the small things that make it easier, then twenty ideas sorted by how much energy you have.
Set the scene in ten minutes

items: **Pick a start time** and put it in your calendar. A plan with a time on it is a plan.
**Move your phone to another room**, or at least to Do Not Disturb, face down.

**Change something small.** Swap the overhead light for a lamp, put on a playlist, light a flameless candle. If you use a real one, set it in a stable holder, keep it at least 12 inches from anything that can burn, never leave it unattended, and skip it in the bedroom.
**Plate the snack.** Not whatever's loose in the cupboard: something you'd be happy to serve a guest.
**Wear the good pajamas.** You're the guest of honor.

body.text: **What makes it easier:** a soft throw, flameless candles and a rechargeable book light, so changing the room takes ten minutes and one trip to the cupboard.

body.title: The night-in kit
body.dek: Small touches that turn a night in into a date: a throw, flameless candles, a book light and a puzzle for the coffee table.

body.text: When you have almost no energy

body.title: Bath and a book
body.note: Run the water, set your book somewhere dry, and stay until the water cools. **What makes it easier:** a rechargeable book light, so you can read in a dim room without reaching for the lamp.

body.title: Home spa hour
body.note: A mask or foot soak if you like them, soft towels, a podcast. Follow the product labels and skip anything that irritates your skin.

body.title: Blanket-fort film night
body.note: Choose a film you've never seen, build a nest of pillows and make the popcorn. No second screen allowed. **What makes it easier:** a soft throw big enough to build a nest with, so the sofa becomes a fort in one pull.

body.title: Audiobook and a puzzle
body.note: The pleasure is in the pairing: busy hands, a gently occupied mind and no decisions. **What makes it easier:** a jigsaw puzzle sized to fit your coffee table, so the pieces are ready the moment the audiobook starts.

body.title: Re-read a favorite
body.note: Choose the book you loved at sixteen or twenty-five and notice what you see in it now. A [reading journal](/journal/how-to-start-a-reading-journal) is a nice place to jot it down. **What makes it easier:** a small reading journal, so what you notice the second time goes straight onto the page.

body.text: When you want something gentle and creative

body.title: Paint by numbers, one color
body.note: Pick one color, fill its areas, then stop. A finished patch of color is the whole date. **What makes it easier:** a small paint-by-number kit with the numbered canvas, paints and a brush in one box; check the listing for what's included.

body.title: Air-dry clay ring dish
body.note: Roll, press and smooth, then leave it to dry for a couple of days (check your clay's label). No kiln needed ([how to start air-dry clay](/journal/how-to-start-air-dry-clay) has more ideas), and it's decorative only, so keep food and drink off it, even if sealed. **What makes it easier:** air-dry clay and a few small acrylic paints, so a ring dish goes from pinch to painted in one place.

body.title: Junk journal your week
body.note: Dig out receipts, tickets and ribbon. Glue three things into a notebook and give each a one-line caption. **What makes it easier:** {{product:stationery-island-a5-blank-journal-180-pages|a blank journal}}, a glue stick and {{product:mr-pen-washi-tape-21-rolls|washi tape}}, so three scraps and three captions become a spread.

body.title: Write a letter you'll actually send
body.note: To a friend, a relative or yourself a year from now. Use real paper. **What makes it easier:** a letter-writing set, so paper, envelopes and a good pen are ready when the mood arrives.

body.title: Calligraphy or hand-lettering practice
body.note: Print a practice sheet, fill a page, then write a favorite song lyric in your neatest handwriting. **What makes it easier:** a set of brush pens, so thick and thin strokes come from one pen.

body.title: Photo-album night
body.note: Pick one trip or one year, choose twelve photos and arrange them in a scrapbook or on a shelf. **What makes it easier:** a photo album or scrapbook, so the twelve photos you choose have somewhere to live.

body.title: For a gentle, creative evening
body.dek: A kit, a journal, a pen or an album arrives ready to use, so the date starts with making rather than shopping.

body.text: When you want to make something delicious

body.title: Dinner for one, properly served
body.note: Choose a recipe you'd cook for a guest. Plate it and eat at the table, napkin and all.

body.title: Bake something and give half away
body.note: A small batch, and a friend or neighbor to hand half to tomorrow. Go by the recipe's timings and keep an eye on it, since ovens vary.

body.title: Mocktail and tea lab
body.note: Choose a classic mocktail or a tea you've never tried and make it properly. Rank your tries if you like; there's no pressure either way. **What makes it easier:** a small tea set or teapot, so the tasting feels like an occasion.

body.text: When you want to feel productive in a nice way

body.title: Plant corner refresh
body.note: Wipe the leaves, repot one plant, move another to better light. If you have pets, check any plant against a pet-safety source first. **What makes it easier:** a small watering can and a pot or two, so the refresh finishes in one go.

body.title: Little extras for the evening
body.dek: A watering can and a pot, a tea set and a small speaker make the kitchen and plant-corner dates feel like occasions.

body.text: A few dates need nothing new. A small extra still makes one nicer, and the rest are fine exactly as they are.

body.title: Make a playlist for a specific mood
body.note: Give it a silly name. Play it start to finish while you tidy a single drawer. **What makes it easier:** a small portable speaker, so the playlist fills the room without headphones.

body.title: Breakfast-for-dinner night
body.note: Pancakes, eggs, a fruit plate. It's a weeknight, and it's a treat.

body.title: Dream-board or plan-the-season session
body.note: Cut out or write down what you want from this season, and pin it where you'll see it daily. **Worth bringing:** old magazines, scissors and {{product:scotch-glue-stick-photo-safe-4-pack|a glue stick}}, if you want to cut and paste rather than write.

body.title: Rearrange one shelf like a boutique
body.note: Books, a plant, a frame and one thrifted object. Step back, then nudge it once more.

body.title: Plan your next outing
body.note: Flip through a list of solo dates, pick one and write it in. A night in that books a night out is a good night.

items: **You keep reaching for your phone.** Put it in a drawer. If it's your music, set the playlist first and turn the screen off.
**You're restless after twenty minutes.** Switch activities. A date can have chapters.
**You feel a bit lonely.** That's normal, and it passes. Text a friend something you're enjoying, or pencil in something social for later in the week.
**You start cleaning instead.** Give the dishes ten minutes on a timer, then come back to your date.

body.text: For more ideas, see [creative hobbies you can start at home](/journal/creative-hobbies-you-can-start-at-home) and [low-energy hobbies](/journal/low-energy-hobbies). Want a new hobby to grow into? See [15 hobbies to start this month](/journal/affordable-hobbies-under-25). Ready to go out instead? Try [30 solo date ideas](/journal/solo-date-ideas) or [how to plan a solo Saturday](/journal/how-to-plan-a-solo-saturday).

Once you've found two or three favorites, rotate them. Give the month a theme, such as clay, cooking or re-reading, and keep a short list on the fridge so that when the evening arrives you pick instead of decide. A cozy night booked in advance also gives you permission to rest. Book it like a plan, even if the plan is a blanket.
